Wayne Gretzky, known as The Great One, is widely regarded as the greatest ice hockey player of all time. A Canadian centre and winger who dominated the sport from the nineteen eighties into the nineteen nineties, he rewrote the NHL record book with unprecedented scoring prowess, winning four Stanley Cups and four Hart Trophies as league MVP.

He scored eight hundred ninety-four NHL goals and one thousand nine hundred sixty-three assists for two thousand eight hundred fifty-seven career points, records that stood unchallenged for decades and may never be broken. Gretzky won the Hart Trophy for MVP four consecutive seasons from nineteen eighty to nineteen eighty-four, a feat unmatched before or since in the modern era. He led the Edmonton Oilers to four Stanley Cups in nineteen eighty-four, nineteen eighty-five, nineteen eighty-seven, and nineteen eighty-eight, establishing the franchise as a dynasty.

He revolutionized play-making and positioning, often positioning himself in the office behind the goal line to create scoring chances rather than pursuing the puck directly. In nineteen eighty-eight, he was traded to the Los Angeles Kings, transforming hockey's popularity on the West Coast and helping legitimize the sport in Southern California. Gretzky played centre and right wing with a low slap-shot style that became iconic and was widely imitated. He holds records for most career assists at one thousand nine hundred sixty-three and most consecutive seasons with forty or more goals.
